hardware_summary: Mixed site. (1) On-site power-generation plant: originally four GE Frame 6 gas turbine-generators (120 MW total), replaced circa 2018-2020 by nine MAN 51/60 gas engines rated 120 MW total, supplying electricity to the LNG facility. (2) Separately, dedicated mechanical-drive gas turbines run the compressor trains: a 280 MW GE Frame 7 gas turbine drives the mixed-refrigerant compression train and a 42 MW GE Frame 6 gas turbine drives the propane compression train (added under Oman LNG's Train 3 / debottlenecking expansion).
fuel_basis: Natural (process/fuel) gas fires both the MAN 51/60 gas engines — explicitly engineered per MAN/LNG Industry to handle 'a variety of differing gas compositions and methane numbers' from the liquefaction process — and the GE Frame 6/7 compressor-drive turbines per GE's own press release.
captive_summary: Oman LNG's Qalhat site carries BOTH captive power forms: a dedicated 120 MW on-site gas-fired power plant (now MAN 51/60 gas engines, replacing the original Frame 6 turbine-generator plant) that supplies the facility's electricity, and separate GE Frame 6/Frame 7 gas turbines that mechanically drive the refrigeration compressor trains.
mechanical_drive_note: GE Frame 7 gas turbine (280 MW) mechanically drives the mixed-refrigerant compression train; GE Frame 6 gas turbine (42 MW) mechanically drives the propane compression train — both supplied under GE's 2004 US$94m contract for Oman LNG's Train 3 expansion at Qalhat.

LNG Industry's report on MAN Energy Solutions' order states MAN 'will equip a new power plant with nine MAN 51/60 gas engines' delivering '120 MW of power to the existing LNG facility of Oman LNG,' replacing 'an existing gas-turbine plant,' engineered to handle Oman LNG's own varying gas composition.

hardware_summary: GE Frame 5C/5D and Frame 9E heavy-frame gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigeration compressor strings across this entity's Ras Laffan trains (the Qatargas-heritage side of the current QatarEnergy LNG structure): the Qatargas II mega-trains use Frame 9E turbines (~132 MW ISO rating) via a Siemens VFD/Ansaldo motor-generator system that can also export surplus electrical power to the plant grid; the earlier trains use GE FR5C/FR5D turbines for both the mixed-refrigerant and propane refrigeration cycles.
fuel_basis: Natural (fuel) gas fires the on-site Frame 5C/5D and Frame 9E gas turbines, per Oil & Gas Journal's technical coverage of the Qatargas II compressor package and Ras Laffan debottlenecking, corroborated by a GASTECH/IGU-style technical paper on Frame 9E start-up co-authored with the operating companies.
captive_summary: This QatarEnergy LNG entity's Ras Laffan trains are the textbook mechanical-drive LNG case: heavy-frame gas turbines (Frame 5C/5D on the older trains, Frame 9E — ~132 MW ISO — on the mega-trains) directly shaft-drive the refrigeration compressors, with the Frame 9E units' motor-generator system also able to export surplus power to the site's internal grid.
mechanical_drive_note: Frame 9E gas turbines (~132 MW ISO each) mechanically drive the mixed-refrigerant/propane/nitrogen refrigeration strings on the mega-trains ('GE Frame 9E as the ideal mechanical driver for the refrigeration strings' — OGJ); earlier trains use GE FR5C/FR5D turbines ('each driven by a General Electric FR5C gas turbine' — OGJ), upgraded to FR5D for a debottlenecking power increase. A technical paper on Frame 9E start-up describes twelve such compressor strings across Qatargas/RasGas Ras Laffan trains providing '100+ megawatt' shaft power plus electrical power export.
confirmed_how: OGJ's 'World's largest LNG compressors designed, tested for Qatargas II' states the GE Frame 9E was 'the ideal mechanical driver for the refrigeration strings' on the Qatargas II mega-trains, customized for variable-speed operation, with a Siemens VFD/Ansaldo motor-generator system that 'allows the turbine to export surplus electrical power to the plant grid.' OGJ's separate 'Qatargas upgrades, debottlenecks Ras Laffan LNG plant' describes the earlier trains: mixed-refrigerant and propane compressors each 'driven by a General Electric FR5C gas turbine,' upgraded to FR5D. A GASTECH/IGU-style technical paper ('Start-Up and Operation of GE Frame 9E,' hosted at pdfcoffee.com) states 'Qatargas and RasGas have successfully completed commissioning, start-up and operation of multiple Frame 9E gas turbine refrigeration strings' across 'twelve of the largest refrigeration compressor strings' at Ras Laffan, which 'provide energy for the propane, mixed refrigerant and nitrogen cooling loops as well as electrical power' to the mega-trains — corroborating both the mechanical-drive and power-export functions industry-wide across the Qatargas/RasGas Ras Laffan complex.
